priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the frozen Claude v23 REJECT (51613328), so v24 answers a finding of mine, and my ACCEPTs in this lineage remain 0 for 3. Codex's HAE23-CX-01 is the second consecutive one I missed, and it landed one step along the axis I had just been working. At v23 I verified each register lane cites the canonical file for its round and lane and treated identity as settled once path, digest, reviewer and subject-name checks were total. But naming a subject is not pinning it: roundLaneIdentity requires the pinned review's subject or reviewOf to name host-effect-authorization.vN, which a review of a superseded vN at a different digest still satisfies. I confirmed the review was the right file and never asked whether it reviewed the round's actual bytes. That is the same error shape I had named one round earlier, confirming a field is constrained without asking which property the constraint pins, so recognising the shape did not stop me repeating it one field over. The refinement I fixed before reading v24 is to follow each identity claim to the artifact it ultimately asserts something about and ask whether that artifact is pinned by bytes or only by name or by another recorded value. That is what produced the finding below, and it is a bounded question rather than an open regress, because a chain that reaches bytes terminates.

shouldFix.title: subjectDigestIdentity terminates the subject-identity chain at a recorded value rather than at bytes, and unlike its sibling clause it does not require the subject file to exist
evidence: The two sibling clauses in the same rule terminate differently. provenanceCheck, which establishes review-file identity, reads 'The path MUST exist as a file; the sha256 of that file's bytes MUST equal the recorded sha256 and the recordedInputs pin'. It has an existence term and a bytes term, so the review chain ends at the file.

subjectDigestIdentity, which establishes subject identity, reads 'predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256 MUST be a 64-hex-lowercase sha256 and MUST equal recordedInputs[docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.vN.json]. Every pinned review for that lane MUST have subjectSha256AtStart and subjectSha256AtEnd as present 64-hex-lowercase strings, both equal to that same digest.' Every term compares one recorded value to another. There is no bytes term and no existence term.

I searched the whole 147294-byte artifact for any clause requiring the vN subject file to exist or its bytes to hash to the pin. Zero clauses. The only string tying recordedInputs to re-measurement is remeasurementClause, which is general prose about cited files and is not wired into registerCoverageRule as a precondition; treating a general clause as discharging a specific mechanical rule is the reasoning I retired at v20 after it produced four under-calls.

So the chain runs: each review's subjectSha256AtStart and AtEnd equal predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256, which equals recordedInputs[vN.json], which equals nothing further. A recordedInputs subject pin that did not match its file would leave every downstream comparison internally consistent and anchored to a digest no file has.

The asymmetry is not incidental to the repair; it is the gap between what Codex asked for and what Codex was after. HAE23-CX-01's requiredRepair says 'Require predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256 to equal recordedInputs[...vN.json]', which v24 implements exactly. But its title is 'The frozen review identity is not bound to the subject bytes it reviewed', and the chain still does not reach bytes for the subject even though it does for the review.

The live corpus is clean, which bounds this to SHOULD-FIX. All eighteen subject files v6 through v23 exist and their bytes reproduce both the recordedInputs pin and the register's subjectSha256, all 74 recordedInputs entries reproduce, and every one of the 36 lane files carries AtStart and AtEnd equal to its round subject.
shouldFix.impact: The purpose of the identity machinery, across six generations of findings, is that a register entry cannot assert something about evidence it is not actually bound to. provenanceCheck achieves that for review files by terminating at the file's bytes. subjectDigestIdentity leaves the subject side anchored to recordedInputs alone, so the strongest statement the rule can make is that several recorded values agree with each other. A wrong or stale subject pin propagates unchallenged through every round entry and every lane's start and end digests, and the mechanical check reports the round complete. That is the same class as the v20 finding where the register asserted a verdict no clause compared to the pinned file, and it is the last unterminated link in a chain the artifact has otherwise closed.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give subjectDigestIdentity the two terms its sibling already has. Require docs/coop/artifacts/host-effect-authorization.vN.json to exist as a file, and require the sha256 of that file's bytes to equal both recordedInputs[that path] and predecessorVerdictFindings[N].subjectSha256, with a missing file or any mismatch refusing before extraction. That terminates the subject chain at bytes exactly as provenanceCheck terminates the review chain, and it is a bounded fix rather than a further link, because a chain anchored in bytes has no next link to check.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Both claimed repairs are delivered and I verified each by execution rather than by reading: registerRoundCompleteness states the obligation I asked for and refuses a dropped middle round, a dropped earliest round and a dropped lane; subjectDigestIdentity refuses Codex's subject-substitution countermodel, which I re-derived myself, along with five malformation probes, and it was made total over v6 and v7 by backfilling rather than by exempting them, which is the scope trap two earlier rules fell into. The full corpus from v6 through v23 passes every stated check with zero failures. The finding comes from the method refinement I fixed before reading the subject, to follow each identity claim to the artifact it asserts something about and ask whether that artifact is pinned by bytes or only by another recorded value. Review-file identity terminates at bytes, because provenanceCheck requires the path to exist and the file's bytes to hash to both the entry digest and the recordedInputs pin. Subject identity does not: subjectDigestIdentity compares recorded values to recorded values, with no bytes term and no existence term, and a search of the whole artifact returns zero clauses supplying either. That leaves the strongest available statement about the subject side as several recorded values agreeing with each other, which is the same class as the v20 finding about an unchecked verdict. It is a bounded fix rather than a further link, because the sibling clause already shows what terminating at bytes looks like, and the live corpus is clean, which is why it is SHOULD-FIX and not a blocker.
